description: Consolidated shared-component decisions extracted from per-page gap answers. Paste into 'Prior gap answers for shared components' slot for all subsequent page analyses.

decisions.decision: Data-loading states use skeleton placeholders with shimmer, NOT the Spinner component. Spinner remains for inline/button loading indicators only.

derived_from.answer: Skeleton rows (3 placeholder rows with shimmer)
Skeleton cards (6 placeholder cards matching card shape with shimmer)
Skeleton cards (3-4 placeholder question cards with shimmer)
Skeleton rows (3 placeholder rows with shimmer)

decisions.decision: Spinner is still used for inline button loading states (e.g., 'Creating...' with disabled button). It is NOT used as the primary page/section loading indicator — skeletons replace that role in the redesign.

API failures use inline error message with Retry button inside the affected section/card — NOT a full-page ErrorBoundary takeover. ErrorBoundary remains as the React error boundary for uncaught JS exceptions only.

derived_from.answer: Inline error message inside the table card with a Retry button
Error banner at top of the form card
Error banner above the card grid with a Retry button (inline)
Inline error banner above question list with Retry button
Inline error message inside the table card with a Retry button

decisions.decision: ErrorBoundary is kept for uncaught React render errors (JS exceptions). It should NOT change visually in the redesign — it is a safety net, not a primary error UX. All user-facing API error states are handled inline per-component.
Buttons in loading state show text change (e.g., 'Create Application' → 'Creating...') with disabled state. No spinner inside button.

derived_from.answer: Button text changes to 'Creating...' with disabled state

decisions.decision: Disabled buttons use reduced opacity + cursor not-allowed. Text may change to indicate in-progress action.
Buttons remain same size/style across breakpoints — no mobile-specific button variants needed.
Skeleton cards (6 placeholder cards matching card shape with shimmer) while hub data loads.
Error banner above the card grid with a Retry button (inline).
Light background tint change on hover.
2 columns on desktop, 1 column on mobile (below md breakpoint).
'Progress' label on left + percentage on right. Visible ProgressBar with percentage replaces current inline spinner approach.
Shows 'Failed X minutes ago' — relative timestamp computed client-side from 'failedAt' in API response.
Keep both aria attributes (aria-valuenow, aria-label) for screen readers AND visible percentage label for sighted users.
Secondary actions (Regenerate, Download, Export, History) render as plain text links with underline on hover.
Add 'soft' prop to Badge for toggling between solid and outlined rendering. Used across all module states (Complete, Ready, Processing, Generating, Failed, Final, Edited, Active).

Hebrew translations required for all new strings: 'View Job Posting', 'Show more', 'Show less', 'Progress', 'Failed X minutes ago', 'Still processing...', 'Generating...', per-module context descriptions.

shared_component_answers.note: Not yet addressed — all 4 routes using ExportDropdown have not been analyzed yet. Questions will be asked during those page analyses.

cross_cutting_patterns.loading: Skeleton placeholders with shimmer (matching container shape) — consistent across all pages. NOT spinner.
cross_cutting_patterns.error_api: Inline error message with Retry button inside the affected card/section — consistent across all pages. NOT full-page error.
cross_cutting_patterns.error_js: ErrorBoundary unchanged — React error boundary for uncaught exceptions only.
cross_cutting_patterns.empty: Table headers visible + centered message + CTA button — consistent for table-based pages.
cross_cutting_patterns.responsive_tables: Tables stack into card layout on mobile — consistent for JobsTable and BaseCVsTable.
cross_cutting_patterns.responsive_sidebar: Icon-only rail on tablet, hamburger overlay on mobile — answered once in /dashboard, applies globally.
cross_cutting_patterns.i18n: Hebrew translations required for all new strings — answered yes on every page.
cross_cutting_patterns.accessibility_tables: Semantic <table> with <thead>/<th>/<tbody>/<tr>/<td> — consistent for all data tables.
